_comment: Known provider pricing pages, so a caller does not have to paste URLs into the
chat. starter_server.py reads this: scrape_websites() with no arguments scrapes
every provider here, and {'groq': ''} resolves the URL from this file.
Passing an explicit {name: url} dict still overrides everything, which is what
Each url below was fetched and checked on the 'verified' date.
display_name is the spelling stored in the database, so the same provider does not appear as both 'deepinfra' and 'DeepInfra'.

cloudrift.note: Prices exactly one model (Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, $0.19 in / $2.37 out). This is the best CloudRift page for token pricing even so — see rejected below.

deepinfra.note: Full named-model table, the richest of the four. DeepSeek-V3 $0.32 in / $0.89 out.

fireworks.note: The rubric URL still resolves and the #serverless-pricing anchor exists, but that page no longer prints per-model prices — it links out to the docs page used here, which does carry the full table.

groq.note: The rubric URL now serves Groq's marketing homepage with no price table — a scrape of it returns marketing copy. The docs model catalogue used here does carry per-million-token prices per named model (GPT OSS 120B $0.15 in / $0.60 out, GPT OSS 20B $0.075 / $0.30). Note it mixes units: some rows are per hour (Whisper Large V3 Turbo, $0.04/hr) or per 1M characters (Orpheus V1, $22.00), which token_plans() drops.

rejected.https://www.cloudrift.ai/pricing: GPU hourly rental only (V100/4090/H100), no per-token prices.
rejected.https://console.groq.com/docs/billing-fa: Explains billing thresholds and cycles only; no prices.
rejected.https://console.groq.com/settings/billin: Requires a logged-in session; not scrapeable.
